text: Since inflammatory markers are normal, ultrasound shows only soft tissue swelling, and MRI indicates intact tendons, this rules out septic arthritis, abscess, and tendon rupture. Does the pain specifically localize to a single tendon or joint, and have you noticed any specific lumps, deformities like a swan-neck or boutonniere position, or a history of psoriasis?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like an acute traumatic event from two days ago. To determine if you have developed a traumatic flexor tendon rupture (often called a "jersey finger") or a mallet finger, can you tell me if you currently have the ability to fully straighten that finger, and have you noticed it drooping at the fingertip or the base of the finger?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Suspected Flexor Digitorum Profundus (FDP) Rupture ("Jersey Finger")

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
